functions.invariant_body:
resp = await client.get(BASE + "/sections")
    sections = resp.json()
    orders = sum(s["orders"] for s in sections)
    sold = sum(s["seats_sold"] for s in sections)
    double_booked = orders - sold - ctx["start_gap"]
    if double_booked <= 0:
        return True, 0, f"All {orders:,} orders got their own seat"
    return False, double_booked, f"Under {CONCURRENCY} concurrent checkouts, {double_booked:,} seats were double-booked"
functions.rationale: Checkouts are spread across all 100 sections so the 100,000-seat arena can't sell out during the run. Each checkout picks the best open seat, awaits the 30 ms payment call, and only then marks the seat sold, so overlapping checkouts in the same section are handed the same seat. Every extra order for a seat that's already sold is a double booking: orders minus seats sold.

functions.request_body:
sections = ctx["sections"]
    return await client.get(BASE + "/sections/" + sections[i % len(sections)] + "/recommendations?party_size=4")
functions.invariant_body:
started = time.monotonic()
    try:
        resp = await client.get(BASE + "/sections/" + ctx["sections"][0] + "/recommendations?party_size=4")
        ok = resp.status_code == 200
    except Exception:
        ok = False
    elapsed_ms = (time.monotonic() - started) * 1000
    samples = ctx["probe_ms"]
    samples.append(elapsed_ms if ok else 10000.0)
    ordered = sorted(samples)
    p95 = ordered[min(len(ordered) - 1, int(len(ordered) * 0.95))]
    slow = sum(1 for s in samples if s > 1000)
    if p95 <= 1000:
        return True, slow, f"Seat recommendations p95 stayed at {p95:,.0f} ms under {CONCURRENCY} concurrent requests"
    return False, slow, f"Under {CONCURRENCY} concurrent requests, seat recommendations p95 hit {p95:,.0f} ms ({slow} of {len(samples)} checks over 1 s)"
functions.rationale: Asks for blocks of four seats across every section at 50 concurrent, while the invariant times one recommendation request on its own client every half second. find_adjacent_blocks scans every open seat for each neighbour, so one 1,000-seat section costs about 1.5 million comparisons of CPU work on the event loop, and concurrent requests queue behind each other. The invariant fails when the p95 of those timed requests goes over 1,000 ms; violations counts the slow checks.
